videos.description: In this keynote at the 2020 Open Education Conference, Jessie Loyer explores how open education can contribute to "Land Back" and other Indigenous sovereignty movements.  Jessie Loyer is Cree-Métis and a member of Michel First Nation. She's a librarian at Mount Royal University in Calgary, on Blackfoot and Treaty 7 territory. Her research looks at Indigenous perspectives on information literacy, supporting language revitalization, and building capacity for oral history sharing and digitization for communities.   Talk delivered on November 12, 2020.

videos.description: New Recruits meet their Drill Instructors on Friday Morning, a day known in Boot Camp as "Black Friday." These speeches are rehearsed by the Drill Instructors and delivered direct, loud, and with full shock value. When that DI yells sit up straight and look at me, every recruit moves without fail.  The SDI Speech is largely the same at each recruit training battalion. A few words in the second paragraph vary from Battalion to Battalion, but all in all, the differences are minimal.    Before the Senior Drill Instructor Speech, recruits receive a speech from their company commander who will introduce him or herself and their First Sergeant (senior enlisted advisor for the Company). Next, they will receive a Speech from their Series Commander, introducing him or herself and their Chief Drill Instructor (senior enlisted advisor for the series). The Series Commander administers the Drill Instructor Oath to the DI's. Upon completion of the oath, the SDI takes over and recites this speech. Once it is over, all hell breaks loose with DI's running up and down the squad bay screaming, throwing things, and generally making everything chaotic.
